businessModel: None disclosed; free, with funding not described on the project pages

summary: A German Chromium modification that stops partial queries and metrics going to central services, blocks Google sign-in and ships stricter defaults. Today it is distributed only as source, so you must build it or rely on distro packages.
bestFor: Linux packagers and builders who want a Chromium with privacy patches
People who value a European, publicly auditable Chromium variant
Readers who want a de-Googled Chromium and can compile it
notFor: Anyone who wants a download-and-run installer or automatic updates
Users who need sync, translation or reliable extension updates
People who want the fastest security-patch cadence

pros.title: Privacy-first defaults
pros.detail: Partial queries, keywords and metrics are not sent to central services without consent; third-party cookies are blocked and DNS prediction is off.

pros.title: Public, auditable source
pros.detail: Full source in a public Git repository under BSD-3-Clause, with reproducible builds claimed.

pros.title: Close Chromium tracking in source
pros.detail: Twelve source releases from Jun to Aug 2026 moved from Chromium 149 to 151.

pros.title: European privacy search default
pros.detail: Qwant has been the default search engine since 2015.

cons.title: No official binaries
cons.detail: The site offers only source tarballs; newer Windows, macOS and Linux builds must be compiled (one reviewer needed over two hours).

cons.title: No auto-update
cons.detail: The browser never updates itself, so users must rebuild or reinstall to receive Chromium security fixes.

cons.title: No sync, limited extensions
cons.detail: Google sign-in and sync are blocked by design, and the extensions panel does not fully work.

cons.title: Slow release flow
cons.detail: Reviews note slow security updates, and nothing newer than 13 Aug 2026 appeared although Chrome 156 shipped on 20 Oct.

faq.q: Can I download Iridium for Windows or macOS?
faq.a: Not from the official site, which currently provides source tarballs only. Third-party download sites list old binaries (2023.09.116), so build from source or use a distro package.

faq.q: How is Iridium different from ungoogled-chromium?
faq.a: Both remove Google integrations; Iridium is run by a German company with a privacy-defaults focus and no built-in blocker, while ungoogled-chromium has a far larger community.
No. You check the version yourself and rebuild or install the newest source release.
